metadata.title: Singapore dbt companies and people for the Singapore dbt Meetup
metadata.purpose: Find Singapore companies using dbt, and people who could speak at or attend the Singapore dbt Meetup.
method: v1 (2026-10-01): one research sub-agent: ~12 web searches (the shared 200-search session cap ran out early), then direct fetches of GovTech STACK [Data] meetup pages (8), Snowflake User Group Singapore pages (5), DataScience SG and Singapore Data & AI Engineering meetup pages via __NEXT_DATA__ (11), PyCon SG 2026 speakers and schedule, PyLadies SG, freehire.me dbt jobs for Singapore (4 pages, 80 ads), TheirStack, Grab tech blog, Medium feeds via rss2json (7 publications), Infinite Lambda case studies, Holistics blog, the getdbt.com sitemap (227 summit and case-study pages), and DEV authors on dbt tags.

Lesson: GovTech's monthly STACK [Data] meetup pages (developer.tech.gov.sg/communities/events/stack-meetups/) list every speaker with title and agency; they are the richest source of Singapore data speakers, though none mentions dbt.

Lesson: freehire.me/jobs?countries=sg&skills=dbt is plain-fetchable and found the direct employers (Endowus, Grasshopper, Secretlab, Traveloka, OCBC, LTA), but half the 80 ads are recruiters with unnamed clients.
Lesson: medium.com/feed returns HTTP 429 to both WebFetch and curl; api.rss2json.com proxies the feed for about 6 publications before it rate-limits too.
Lesson: no getdbt.com dbt Summit or case-study page (227 checked) names a Singapore company, and the dbt World Tour has APAC stops in Sydney, Melbourne, Auckland and Tokyo but not Singapore.
Lesson: Infinite Lambda's case studies name Singapore dbt users (Mandai Wildlife Group, Keppel) that no job ad shows.
Lesson: meetup.com group pages give past events through __NEXT_DATA__; DataScience SG has moved to luma.com/datascienceSG, which renders empty when fetched.

v1 (2026-10-01): location pass. 17 people placed from public pages (Meetup hosts and RSVPs, GitHub, speaker bios, author boxes, recent in-person talks at a local-office employer) and LinkedIn search results (6 of them),, or from the same person's located record in another chapter's file, by the evidence rules in research/README.md. Each placed person has a 'location (high|medium)' note and evidence link. 14 people are still unknown.

v2 (2026-10-01): women-in-data pass with fetches only (no web search, about 12 fetches): Meetup gql2 groupSearch near Singapore with 18 queries, then the past events of Women Devs SG, Singapore WiMLDS and R-Ladies Singapore; the GDG Singapore events API (Women Techmakers IWD events); WiDS site search and the two WiDS Singapore event pages; She Loves Data and Girls in Tech Singapore. A WiDS Taipei talk by a Singapore-based Databricks engineer was found in the Taipei pass. 7 people added (1 speaker and 6 connectors), plus organiser evidence for one existing person. Nobody's gender is recorded or inferred; no pronouns were self-published.
Lesson: Women Devs SG is Singapore's most active women-in-tech group on Meetup, but its event pages rarely name speakers. The hosts are the useful contacts.

Lesson: Women Techmakers Singapore runs its International Women's Day events through GDG Singapore (gdg.community.dev chapter 495). The 2024 and 2025 events had AI workshops and fireside chats, with no names in the agenda.
Lesson: She Loves Data, founded in Singapore, now runs global online AI courses; its events page returns 404 and no Singapore events are listed.

v3 (2026-10-01): company pass with fetches only (no web search, about 25 fetches): the MyCareersFuture API (7 searches, 551 ads, 36 with the whole word dbt), the freehire.me open API (skills=dbt, countries=SG, 200 ads, full text read where the search result was cut), Greenhouse, Lever and Ashby boards for about 100 regional employers, Hacker News Who is hiring through Algolia (3 queries), and the getdbt.com case-study text file.

Lesson: the MyCareersFuture API (api.mycareersfuture.gov.sg/v2/jobs?search=...) answers a plain fetch with full ad text, the employer's registered name and the posting date. A search for dbt finds only 36 ads; searching data engineer, snowflake and bigquery and filtering the text for dbt found no more.

Lesson: the freehire.me JSON API (freehire.me/api/v1/jobs/search?skills=dbt&countries=SG) returns all 200 Singapore dbt-tagged ads in two calls; the search results cut the ad at about 1,000 characters, so read /api/v1/jobs/<slug> for the rest.
Lesson: most Singapore tech employers (Grab, Shopee, Carousell, ShopBack, PropertyGuru, Endowus) have no public Greenhouse, Lever or Ashby board; Airwallex, Workato, Coinhako and Thunes do.

v3 (2026-10-01): 25 LinkedIn profiles taken from pages already tied to each person (event, speaker and author pages, GitHub social accounts) with research/harvest_linkedin.py, without searching. Page links are medium confidence, GitHub links high.

field_definitions.metadata.schema_version: shared schema version used by every <region>_dbt_companies.json file (see research/README.md §4)
field_definitions.companies.type: employer | consultancy | vendor | outsourcing | recruiter | community | independent | other
field_definitions.companies.watchlist: true for companies checked but not yet showing in-region dbt work (unconfirmed local presence, or weak/none dbt signal); kept so they are not re-researched
field_definitions.companies.excluded_from_outreach: true for companies deliberately not approached (e.g. dbt Labs staff who already speak regularly)
field_definitions.companies.local_presence: confirmed | not_confirmed | none — whether the company has people/roles in the region
field_definitions.companies.dbt_signal: strong = public post/case study/talk, or dbt required / core stack in a job ad; medium = dbt listed among alternatives, tagged by a job board's skill extraction, or seen only in a snippet; nice-to-have = listed as a plus; weak = unverified; none = stack appears to be non-dbt, or not applicable
field_definitions.companies.other_evidence.type: article | talk | case_study | oss | job_posting | careers | company_blog | conference_talk | meetup | podcast | news | profile | blog_scanned (blog checked, even if nothing relevant) | other
field_definitions.companies.job_postings.dbt_mentioned_in_: true = dbt seen in the ad text (or tagged from the text by the job board); null = only seen in a search snippet about the ad
field_definitions.companies.job_postings.posted_date: date shown on the job board (YYYY-MM-DD), null if unknown
field_definitions.companies.job_postings.last_seen: last run in which the ad was still listed
field_definitions.companies.job_postings.job_family / work: as labelled by the job board (e.g. Analytics Engineer; Remote/Hybrid/On-site); null if not labelled
field_definitions.companies.people.id: kebab-case ASCII name, stable across runs
field_definitions.companies.people.city / based_in_region: city as seen publicly; based_in_region true = evidence they are in the region, false = evidence elsewhere, null = unverified
field_definitions.companies.people.level: leadership if the title contains Head/Director/VP/Chief/Founder/C-level/Manager/Lead, otherwise working
field_definitions.companies.people.confidence: High = name + title + company visible in a public source; Medium = indirect evidence; Low = weak evidence
field_definitions.companies.people.linkedin_confidence: high = name + company/role in the search result title; medium = indirect or name variant; low = searched, not found; not_searched
field_definitions.companies.people.profile_urls: other public professional profiles where the person can be reached, as [{type, url, source}]: type is one of github, meetup, zenn, qiita, velog, medium, devto, substack, ithome, sessionize, x, bluesky, website, note; source is the page that ties the profile to the person. never an email address or phone number
field_definitions.companies.people.mentions_dbt: true if any of the person's public content (or profile snippet) mentions dbt; false if content found without dbt; null if unknown
field_definitions.companies.people.meetup_fit.speaker_pote: high = has given a dbt talk, 2+ public talks, spoke at this chapter before, or priority_tier 1; medium = some public content; low = none found
field_definitions.companies.people.meetup_fit.attendee_pot: high = in region and public dbt content (or confirmed practitioner at a strong-dbt company); medium = in-region/unknown data practitioner; low = outside the region or weak identification
field_definitions.companies.people.internal_vinted: true for Vinted colleagues (kept for completeness, not outreach targets)
field_definitions.companies.people.priority_tier: 1 = strong recent lead: a proven speaker with a relevant recent talk, or an emerging_voice in (or not known to be outside) the region with authored content from 2024 onwards; 2 = good lead / needs verification / older content / relevant talk at another meetup; 3 = peripheral, off-topic or remote; organiser / backup / connector = special roles
field_definitions.companies.people.past_chapter_talks: talks this person gave at this chapter's own meetups, matched by name
field_definitions.companies.people.speaker_evidence.type: talk | panel | podcast | article | case_study | oss | interview | organiser | host | post | profile
field_definitions.companies.people.speaker_evidence.topics: 1-3 topics, most relevant first, only from metadata.topic_vocabulary (pipeline/enrich.py::TOPIC_VOCABULARY); organiser/host/profile entries are tagged 'community'
field_definitions.companies.people.speaker_evidence.conten: stable id; an item with several authors appears under each of them with the same content_id
field_definitions.companies.people.speaker_evidence.url_pr: direct = the item itself; overview_page = a listing/homepage where the item appears
field_definitions.past_meetups.talks.topics: 1-3 topics, most relevant first, only from metadata.topic_vocabulary (pipeline/enrich.py::TOPIC_VOCABULARY); organiser/host/profile entries are tagged 'community'
field_definitions.companies.people.lead_type: proven_speaker = has given a talk, panel or podcast, or spoke at this chapter; emerging_voice = has authored public content (blog post, article, newsletter, open-source project, LinkedIn post) but no talk found yet — a priority for first-time speaker invitations; featured = only quoted or profiled in someone else's content (case study, interview, team feature); no_public_content = none found
field_definitions.companies.people.pronouns: pronouns exactly as the person publishes them (e.g. on a speaker listing, bio or profile headline); null when not self-stated. Never inferred from names, photos or third-person wording
field_definitions.companies.people.sourced_via: channels through which the person was found (list): company_blog_scan | case_study | conference_or_meetup_agenda | data_berlin_meetup | women_in_data_community | chapter_meetup_history | newsletter_or_blog | podcast | github | linkedin_search | job_ad_company_search | other

caveats: Titles, employers and cities come from public pages/snippets and are often inferred from the employer's HQ - verify before outreach.
Only public professional information is recorded; no personal contact details. Pronouns only when self-stated.
Very few Singapore people publish about dbt. Most leads here are data engineers who spoke about pipelines, data mesh or semantic layers; ask each whether they use dbt.
The emerging-voice rule raises Grab and foodpanda blog authors to tier 1 even though their posts do not mention dbt; treat them as first-time speakers on a data topic.

Gender was not inferred. The GovTech STACK series has many speakers who may help balance a line-up; confirm with organisers who know them. PyLadies Singapore and Women Devs SG are the women-in-tech communities found.
The web-search budget ran out after about 12 searches, so Coalesce/dbt Summit speaker lists, Databricks and Snowflake World Tour Singapore agendas, and LinkedIn were not covered.

LinkedIn: 9 of 82 people have a profile url, taken word for word from search results. 73 were never searched (linkedin_confidence 'not_searched'); the 2026-10-01 pass searched the best-ranked leads with no known location first.
Speakers and organisers from women-in-data community events are recorded by where they spoke or organised (sourced_via women_in_data_community). No one's gender is recorded or inferred.
Employers and dbt wording come from public job ads on 2026-10-01; ads close, so check the employer before outreach.
Recruiter ads rarely name the client. A role listed under a recruiter does not show which company uses dbt.
A remote ad, an ad in French and ads where DBT means something else (digital business transformation) were left out.
